_note: 科研時事（站點級，跨科目）。顯示在三科總覽頁。cat 用 bio/chem/phys/math，只影響標籤顏色。越新的排越前。內容必須來自可靠來源並附連結——時事不是常識，寧可少寫也不要編。本檔由 scripts/fetch_news.py 自動抓取泛科學 RSS 產生，可手動補充。

items.t: 科學家粉碎氧核以重建大爆炸中的物質
items.x: 科學家以接近光速的速度碰撞氧原子核，重建了宇宙誕生之初物質的原始狀態。令人驚訝的結果表明，這種奇異物質可以在比之前證明的更小、能量更低的碰撞中形成，挑戰了早期宇宙物理學的已知界限。
items.orig: Scientists smash oxygen nuclei to recreate matter from the Big Bang
items.origX: Scientists have recreated a primordial state of matter from the dawn of the universe by colliding oxygen nuclei at nearly the speed of light. The surprising results show that this exotic substance can form in smaller, lower-energy collisions than previously demonstrated, challenging the known boundaries of early-universe physics.

items.t: 科學家發現金屬可以抵抗 -424°F 的深度冷凍
items.x: 科學家發現了一種令人驚訝的機制，可以使某些金屬在低至 -253°C (-424°F) 的溫度下抵抗開裂，而此時類似的材料通常會變得非常脆弱。兩種實驗合金沒有斷裂，而是重新組織了內部結構，創造了吸收壓力和保持靈活性的新方法。
items.orig: Scientists discover metals that defy the deep freeze at -424°F
items.origX: Scientists have discovered a surprising mechanism that allows certain metals to resist cracking at temperatures as low as -253°C (-424°F), when similar materials typically become dangerously brittle. Instead of breaking, two experimental alloys reorganize their internal structures, creating new ways to absorb stress and remain flexible.

items.t: 晶體中的微小缺陷揭示了巨大的量子驚喜
items.x: 研究人員解決了一個長期存在的挑戰，即了解鑽石和碳化矽等材料中的微小缺陷在光照下如何表現。他們的新計算方法揭示了碳化矽中一個令人驚訝的重要能量損失機制，而科學家之前卻低估了這個機制。這項發現有助於解釋多年來困擾研究人員的謎團，
items.orig: A tiny defect in a crystal reveals a big quantum surprise
items.origX: Researchers have solved a long-standing challenge in understanding how tiny defects in materials like diamond and silicon carbide behave when exposed to light. Their new computational method revealed a surprisingly important energy-loss mechanism in silicon carbide that scientists had previously underestimated. The finding helps explain a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years and could improve the design of quantum computers and sensors.

items.t: 科學家發現了一個可以引發或破壞化學反應的隱藏因素
items.x: 研究人員發現了一個可以決定化學反應成功或失敗的隱藏因素，然後利用它將所需產物的比例從 16% 提高到 97%。透過控制電極附近的酸度，他們開發了一種很有前途的方法，使用氧氣和電力而不是添加危險的氧化劑來製造塑膠、藥品和其他產品的化學物質。
items.orig: Scientists discover a hidden factor that can make or break chemical reactions
items.origX: Researchers discovered a hidden factor that can determine whether chemical reactions succeed or fail, and then used it to boost the proportion of the desired product from 16% to 97%. By controlling acidity near electrodes, they developed a promising way to manufacture chemicals for plastics, medicines, and other products using oxygen and electricity instead of hazardous added oxidants.

items.t: 科學家揭示了隱藏的蛇咬傷危機，每年導致多達 513,000 人死亡
items.x: 一項令人震驚的新研究表明，全世界因毒蛇咬傷而死亡的人數遠遠多於官方統計數字，估計每年有 274,000 至 513,000 人死亡。研究人員發現，每年有多達 700 萬人遭受蛇毒攻擊，而超過 80 萬名倖存者會留下長期殘疾。
items.orig: Scientists reveal a hidden snakebite crisis killing up to 513,000 people a year
items.origX: A startling new study suggests that venomous snakebites are killing far more people worldwide than official statistics indicate, with an estimated 274,000 to 513,000 deaths every year. Researchers found that as many as 7 million people could suffer snake envenoming annually, while more than 800,000 survivors are left with long-term disabilities.

items.t: 科學家發現有毒火蠑螈的秘密發光
items.x: 研究人員在歐洲常見的黑黃火蠑螈中發現了一種令人驚訝的隱藏能力：它們在紫外線下發出綠色和青色的光。這種神秘的螢光主要來自於它們皮膚上的腺體和有毒的分泌物，釋放後可以持續發光24小時以上。
items.orig: Scientists discover a secret glow in toxic fire salamanders
items.origX: Researchers have discovered a surprising hidden ability in Europe's familiar black-and-yellow fire salamanders: they glow green and cyan under ultraviolet light. The mysterious fluorescence comes mainly from glands in their skin and their toxic secretions, which can continue glowing for more than 24 hours after being released.

items.t: 科學家剛剛打破了物理學教科書的規則
items.x: 科學家們透過產生比傳統理論預測的能量高得多的 X 射線來挑戰雷射物理學的長期規則。這項令人驚訝的發現揭示了兩個電子如何協同工作可以克服先前公認的極限，為量子研究開闢新的可能性。
items.orig: Scientists just broke a textbook rule of physics
items.origX: Scientists have defied a long-standing rule of laser physics by generating X-rays with much higher energies than conventional theory predicts. The surprising discovery reveals how two electrons working together can overcome a previously accepted limit, opening new possibilities for quantum research.

items.t: 革命性的新型顯微鏡可以揭示隱藏的生命機制
items.x: 研究人員開發了一種革命性的顯微鏡，它使用極其強大的激光，使以前看不見的細胞結構變得更容易看到。該技術極大地提高了影像清晰度，使科學家能夠檢查傳統電子顯微鏡難以捕捉的小蛋白質。它最終可能揭示微小的分子機器如何在細胞內相互作用，前提是
items.orig: A revolutionary new microscope could reveal the hidden machinery of life
items.origX: Researchers have developed a revolutionary microscope that uses an incredibly powerful laser to make previously invisible cellular structures easier to see. The technology dramatically improves image clarity, allowing scientists to examine small proteins that conventional electron microscopes struggle to capture. It could eventually reveal how tiny molecular machines interact inside cells, providing an unprecedented look at the hidden workings of life.

items.t: 小行星殺死了恐龍。鱷魚為何能存活？
items.x: 科學家可能已經解開了一個 6600 萬年前的謎團：鱷魚如何在滅絕恐龍的小行星中倖存下來。對化石和古代氣候的全面分析表明，它們對溫暖環境的偏好使它們處於熱帶避難所，即使在災難性影響之後，這些避難所仍然適合居住。
items.orig: The asteroid killed the dinosaurs. Why did crocodiles survive?
items.origX: Scientists may have solved a 66-million-year-old mystery: how crocodiles survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs. A sweeping analysis of fossils and ancient climates suggests that their preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that remained habitable even after the catastrophic impact.
